newsitem.title: USA: Montana seeding aided by drying winds, rain needed.
newsitem.headline: Montana seeding aided by drying winds, rain needed.

text.p: Warm, dry weather allowed crop planting to accelerate in Montana during the week ended May 18, the Montana agricultural statistics service said.

There were 6.9 days suitable for fieldwork, with winds assisting the drying of soils. Planting pace caught up with or moved ahead of averages but falling soil moisture was also beginning to cause concern for germination, it said.

Pasture and range was rated 40 percent good to excellent, versus 49 percent a week earlier. Topsoil moisture was rated 25 percent very short, 39 pct short, 35 pct adequate; subsoils were rated 13 pct very short, 26 pct short, 59 pct adequate.

Spring wheat was 78 percent planted, up from 62 percent a week earlier and 74 pct last year but behind the five-year average of 84 percent. Emergence was at 45 pct versus only 12 last week, 26 last year and 50 percent on average.
Winter wheat was rated 37 percent good to excellent, versus 56 percent at that level a week ago. Winter wheat was rated 49 pct fair vs 32 a week ago.
Barley planted 84 pct vs 60 week ago, 74 year ago, 82 avg.
Barley emerged 35 pct vs 8 w/a, 28 y/a, 47 avg.
Corn planted 81 pct vs 54 week ago, 64 year ago, 69 avg.
Corn emerged 8 pct vs 1 w/a, 16 y/a, avg unavailable.
Oats planted 68 pct vs 48 w/a, 52 y/a, 74 avg.
Oats emerged 36 pct vs 13 w/a, 19 y/a, 41 avg.
Sugarbeets planted 98 pct vs 94 w/a, 94 y/a, 97 avg.
Sugarbeets planted 74 pct vs 47 w/a, 59 y/a, avg unavail.
